Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

A **finite quantizer** on a measurable space is a measurable map into a finite set. Let X,Y,Z be standard-Borel random elements. Choose sequences of finite quantizers $q_n$ on X and $r_n$ on Y whose generated sigma-algebras increase to the full sigma-algebras of their respective spaces. Then
$$I(X;Y)=\lim_{n\to\infty}I(q_n(X);r_n(Y))$$
and
$$I(X;Y\mid Z)=\lim_{n\to\infty}I(q_n(X);r_n(Y)\mid Z).$$
Such sequences exist by countable generation of standard-Borel sigma-algebras. In the conditional formula, Z remains unchanged.

Let $(E,\mathcal E)$ and $(F,\mathcal F)$ be measurable spaces and let $P$ be a probability measure on $(E\times F,\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal F)$. Its marginals are $P_E(A)=P(A\times F)$ and $P_F(B)=P(E\times B)$. The product probability $P_E\otimes P_F$ exists by the finite product-measure theorem. Define the **measure-theoretic mutual information** of the joint law $P$ by
$$I(P):=D(P\|P_E\otimes P_F)\in[0,+\infty].$$
For random elements $X,Y$ with joint law $P_{XY}$, write $I(X;Y):=I(P_{XY})$. The logarithm convention is the natural logarithm, so finite values are in nats as fixed by [[def-it-information-units-and-logarithm-base]]. The divergence is directional in its two law arguments and is $+\infty$ when $P_{XY}\not\ll P_X\otimes P_Y$.

This definition uses only the joint law, not a choice of density or a difference of entropy quantities.

changes.original_value:
Let X,Y,Z be random elements with standard-Borel value spaces and joint law $P_{XYZ}$. Let $K(z,\cdot)$ and $L(z,\cdot)$ be regular conditional laws of X and Y given Z=z. Let R be the probability law on the product space whose rectangle values are
$$R(C\times A\times B)=\int_C K(z,A)L(z,B)\,P_Z(dz).$$
Its existence, uniqueness, and independence of the versions K,L are established in [[lem-same-marginal-conditional-product-law-well-defined]]. Define the **conditional mutual information** by
$$I(X;Y\mid Z):=D(P_{XYZ}\|R)\in[0,+\infty].$$
The reference R has the same Z marginal as the joint law and makes X,Y independent conditionally on Z. The logarithm is natural, so finite values are measured in nats under [[def-it-information-units-and-logarithm-base]]. The definition is a divergence between full probability laws; it does not subtract two possibly infinite entropies.

Assume AC. Let X,Y,Z be random elements with standard-Borel value spaces and write $P_{ZXY}$ for the joint law of $(Z,X,Y)$ in that coordinate order. Let $K(z,\cdot)$ and $L(z,\cdot)$ be regular conditional laws of X and Y given Z=z. Let R be the probability law on the same product space whose rectangle values are
$$R(C\times A\times B)=\int_C K(z,A)L(z,B)\,P_Z(dz).$$
Its existence, uniqueness, and independence of the versions K,L are established in [[lem-same-marginal-conditional-product-law-well-defined]]. Define the **conditional mutual information** by
$$I(X;Y\mid Z):=D(P_{ZXY}\|R)\in[0,+\infty].$$
The reference R has the same Z marginal as the joint law and makes X,Y independent conditionally on Z. The logarithm is natural, so finite values are measured in nats under [[def-it-information-units-and-logarithm-base]]. The definition is a divergence between full probability laws; it does not subtract two possibly infinite entropies.

Put $V_{n,p}=W_{n,n-2p}(\mathbb C,q+q^{-1})$, $R_{n,p}=\operatorname{rad}\phi_{n,n-2p}$ and $L_{n,p}=V_{n,p}/R_{n,p}$, allowing $L_{2p,p}=0$ when $\delta=0$. Let $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)\ge2$. For a noncritical label write $n-2p+1=k\kappa+r$ with $1\le r<\kappa$. Then
$$\dim R_{n,p}=\begin{cases}\dim L_{n,p+r-\kappa},&p+r-\kappa\ge0,\\0,&p+r-\kappa<0.\end{cases}$$
More explicitly, set the dimensions of out-of-range modules to zero. At critical labels $\dim R_{n,p}=0$. At noncritical labels,
$$\dim R_{n,p}=\begin{cases}\dim R_{n-1,p}+\dim V_{n-1,p-1},&r=\kappa-1,\\\dim R_{n-1,p}+\dim R_{n-1,p-1},&r\ne\kappa-1.\end{cases}$$
The initial condition is $\dim R_{n,0}=0$. These formulas include $\kappa=2$ and the zero-form perfect-matching module.

Use the digits and place values in [[def-temperley-lieb-spencer-digit-support]], and write $N+1=\sum_{j=0}^r n_js_j$ with $n_r>0$. When $\ell<\infty$, each signed expression $\sum_j\varepsilon_jn_js_j-1$ with $\varepsilon_r=1$ lies in $[0,N]$, has parity $N$, and determines its signs at every nonzero digit uniquely. Thus the support has $2^h$ elements, where $h$ is the number of nonzero digits below $r$.

For $0\le v\le u$, the specialized quantum binomial $B_{u,v}(\delta)$ is nonzero exactly when each mixed-radix digit of $v$ is at most the corresponding digit of $u$. In characteristic zero this uses the two digits with places $1,\ell$; if $\ell=\infty$, every such binomial is nonzero.

For any $0<k\le r$, changing all signs at indices less than $k$ reflects the corresponding support element about the wall $H-1$, where $H=\sum_{j\ge k}\varepsilon_jn_js_j$ is a positive multiple of $s_k$. In particular, writing $L=\sum_{j<k}\varepsilon_jn_js_j$ gives the pair $H+L-1,H-L-1$ and $|L|<s_k$.

Let $a,b,c$ belong to this support, and suppose their sets of negative nonzero digits satisfy $A\subseteq B\subseteq C$. Then $a\ge b\ge c$ and the specialized quantum binomial
$$B_{(a-c)/2,(a-b)/2}(\delta)$$
is nonzero. Here $B$ denotes the polynomial quantum binomial of [[lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion]]. If $\ell=\infty$, the same last assertion holds for the only triple $a=b=c=N$.

For the established standard $\ell=4$ root-of-unity ribbon quotient, the labels are $0,1,2$, the dimensions are $(1,\sqrt2,1)$, and

$$S=\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&\frac1{\sqrt2}&\frac12\\[2pt]\frac1{\sqrt2}&0&-\frac1{\sqrt2}\\[2pt]\frac12&-\frac1{\sqrt2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}, \quad(\theta_0,\theta_1,\theta_2)=(1,e^{3\pi i/8},-1).$$

The fusion products are $1\otimes1=0\oplus2$, $1\otimes2=1$, and $2\otimes2=0$; the torus state dimension is $3$.
